about: How `delegate` (the NLI skill) decides where a target goes (2026-09-27, the a2a-delegate lane of the gap-closure build). A target is one of three things, decided in this order by one pure function in each SDK (TypeScript src/skills/nli/a2a-target.ts `classifyDelegateTarget`, Python webagents/agents/skills/robutler/nli/a2a_target.py `classify_delegate_target`): `peer`, a URL the agent file's `a2a.peers` configures (the longest configured URL that is the target or a path prefix of it, whatever its scheme, since the owner wrote it); `probe`, an https URL off the platform's origin, whose `/.well-known/agent-card.json` (then `/.well-known/agent.json`) is fetched once and, when it names an A2A 1.0 JSON-RPC interface, called over A2A; `platform`, everything else (`@name`, a bare name, the platform's own agents by URL, plain http), which keeps the platform path unchanged: the per-hop budget, the child token and the receipt. A peer hop carries the peer's configured bearer and nothing else: never the run's payment token, the caller's auth token, an owner assertion or the agent's platform key (`never_sent_headers`). A redirect is refused by the client. A card whose signature names a `jku` must verify (`verification`); an unsigned card is called unverified. Nobody pays for a peer hop, and the result says so (`unpaid_note`). Read by typescript/tests/unit/skills/nli-a2adelegate.test.ts and python/tests/test_nli_a2adelegate.py.

cases.name: an @name is an agent on the platform
a bare name is an agent on the platform
a slash without a scheme is the legacy path
the platform's own agent by URL keeps the platform path
the platform origin compares without case or a default port
a trailing slash is the same peer
a peer configured without a token is called with none
a configured peer on loopback is trusted because the owner wrote it
a configured peer wins over the platform origin: the owner asked for A2A
a look-alike host is not a peer; it is probed
an https URL off the platform is probed for a card
the probe URL loses its trailing slash
whitespace around the target is ignored
plain http off the platform is never probed
an unconfigured loopback URL is never probed
a URL that is not http(s) is the legacy path
an empty target is the legacy path, which refuses it

probe.about: One card fetch per delegate to an https URL off the platform, the client's discovery walk (`vectors.json` `client.card_paths`), bounded by `timeout_seconds`. A card that names an A2A 1.0 JSON-RPC interface routes the hop over A2A with no bearer; anything else (404 at both paths, no such interface, an unreachable host, a redirect) leaves the target on the platform path exactly as before.

verification.about: A card whose signature names a `jku` is verified against it before the hop (`verify_card` `jku` in both clients): the key set is fetched only from an origin the card is tied to, over https unless the peer is on loopback. A card that does not verify refuses the hop with the client's sentence. A card with no signature, or a signature naming no `jku` (OpenClaw's), is called unverified and the hop proceeds.
verification.refused: the card at {card_url} does not verify: {reason}

unpaid_note: [delegate over A2A: {url} is a peer outside the platform, paid by nobody: no budget applies to this hop and there is no receipt]
attachments_refused: delegation to {url} refused: attachments cannot be forwarded to a peer outside the platform; put the content in the message or send it another way

result.about: The hop's reply, then `unpaid_note` on its own line; an empty reply is `(no response)`. TypeScript returns a structured result whose `data.a2a` carries `url`, `rpcUrl`, `taskId`, `state` and `verified` (true, false, or null for an unsigned card); Python's tool returns the text alone, as every `nli_tool` result is a string.
